_comment: Statically linked XDK library functions known by name, with the address each known title has them at (hex, image addresses only: no code). library: D3D (the Xbox 360 Direct3D runtime), CRT, XAudio, XACT, XMA, XGraphics, XInput, XUI. Sources: The Simpsons Game port's re/native_renderer_plan.md (xdk_sigs matches against the Conan-era signature set), the Crackdown port's HLE renderer plan (the D3D runtime range 0x826A0000-0x826D0000 is not named per function yet). The CRT entries come from the ports' own native replacements and from tools/library_scan.py (the same function found in another title). Grows with signature matching (milestone L4); tools/build_db.py reads it into db/xdk.json.

functions.name: memcpy
functions.note: the long forward copy; leaves its destination register (64 bits) at r1 - 8. Any360: xdk::CrtMemcpy, the one function the three titles bind (docs/NATIVE_FUNCTIONS.md)

functions.name: memcpy (plain forward copy)
functions.note: bytes to alignment, then words; the same instructions in the three titles. Any360: xdk::CrtCopyForward, bound in the three

functions.name: memset
functions.note: Any360: xdk::CrtMemset, the one function the three titles bind (docs/NATIVE_FUNCTIONS.md)

functions.name: memmove
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles: memcpy below the source (signed compare), a backward copy above it. Any360: xdk::CrtMemmove, bound in the three

functions.name: wcslen
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles. Any360: xdk::CrtWcslen, bound in Test Drive Unlimited and Crackdown (The Simpsons Game: no run has called it)

functions.name: strchr
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles. Any360: xdk::CrtStrchr, bound in the three

functions.name: strncmp
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles. Any360: xdk::CrtStrncmp, bound in the three

functions.name: strncpy
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles. Any360: xdk::CrtStrncpy, bound in the three

functions.name: strrchr
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles. Any360: xdk::CrtStrrchr, bound in the three

functions.name: strncat
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles. Any360: xdk::CrtStrncat, bound in the three

functions.name: wcscpy
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles. Any360: xdk::CrtWcscpy, bound in Test Drive Unlimited and Crackdown (The Simpsons Game: no run has called it)

functions.name: wcsncpy
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles. Any360: xdk::CrtWcsncpy, bound in Crackdown (the two others: no run has called it)

functions.name: tolower
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles (the C locale's). Any360: xdk::CrtTolower, bound in Test Drive Unlimited and Crackdown (The Simpsons Game: no run has called it)

functions.name: toupper
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles (the C locale's). Any360: xdk::CrtToupper, bound in Test Drive Unlimited (the two others: no run has called it)

functions.name: wcscmp
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles: -1, 0 or 1. Any360: xdk::CrtWcscmp, bound in Crackdown and The Simpsons Game (Test Drive Unlimited: no run has called it)

functions.name: mbtowc
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles: the C locale's, a byte is a character. Any360: xdk::CrtMbtowc, bound in Crackdown (the two others: no run has called it)

functions.name: strlen (loop of bytes)
functions.note: Havok's own, inside its code in the three titles: middleware, kept as it is. Any360 has xdk::CrtStrlen for the value (checked in Crackdown); bound in no title

functions.name: strcmp (loop of bytes)
functions.note: Havok's own, inside its code in the three titles: the difference of the first bytes that differ. Any360 has xdk::CrtStrcmp for the value (checked in Test Drive Unlimited); bound in no title

functions.name: GetLastError
functions.note: the thread's last error (thread + 352, the thread named by r13 + 256; 0 while r13 + 336 is not zero). Any360: xdk::XapiGetLastError, checked in the three and bound in none: five instructions, no gain as a host routine

functions.name: SetLastError
functions.note: stores the thread's last error (nothing while r13 + 336 is not zero). Any360: xdk::XapiSetLastError, checked in the three and bound in none: no gain as a host routine

functions.name: _stricmp
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles: the difference of the first bytes that differ, A to Z lowered; at the second string's end the first's byte as it is. Any360: xdk::CrtStricmp, bound in the three

functions.name: strstr
functions.note: the same instructions in the three titles. Any360: xdk::CrtStrstr (the host's search once both strings end in plain memory), bound in the three

functions.name: _finite
functions.note: 1 unless the double's exponent is all ones. Any360: xdk::CrtFinite, bound in The Simpsons Game (the two others: no run has called it)

functions.name: _isnan
functions.note: Any360: xdk::CrtIsnan, bound in Crackdown (the two others: no run has called it)

functions.name: _sptype
functions.note: 1 plus infinity, 2 minus infinity, 3 quiet NaN, 4 signalling NaN, 0 otherwise. Any360: xdk::CrtSptype, bound in no title (no run has called it)

functions.name: _get_exp
functions.note: the exponent field less 1022 (in the image twice in Test Drive Unlimited and The Simpsons Game). Any360: xdk::CrtGetExp, bound in the three

functions.name: _set_exp
functions.note: the double with its exponent field made r4 + 1022 (in the image twice in Test Drive Unlimited and The Simpsons Game). Any360: xdk::CrtSetExp, bound in the three

functions.name: _add_exp
functions.note: the double with r4 added to its exponent field. Any360: xdk::CrtAddExp, bound in no title (no run has called it; Crackdown keeps its own copy)

functions.name: XMemCpy
functions.note: the XDK's vector copy next to XAPI: 16-byte vectors, dcbt ahead of the source, dcbz128 ahead of the destination; named after what it does (its name is not in the titles). Three builds of the same steps. Any360: xdk::XMemCpy for ranges that do not overlap, bound in the three

functions.name: D3D GPU wait step
functions.note: the step every wait of the D3D runtime for the GPU loops on (eight db16cyc, the device's stop flag, the ring's read pointer, the hang check after about five seconds); named after what it does. Call of Duty: Black Ops has it at 0x824B3F38. Any360: xdk::D3dGpuWait (sleeps on the GPU's progress count after the step's own code), bound in Test Drive Unlimited and The Simpsons Game; Crackdown's port keeps its own hook (blocks on the words the GPU writes)
